headline: On last trading day, Sensex dropped over 300 points as inflation and crude oil concerns weighed on markets.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 16 November.

why: Sensex and Nifty slipped on the last session due to inflation concerns and rising crude oil pressures.
Profit booking emerged after benchmark indices registered strong mid-week gains.
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reported a Q2 net loss of ₹5,531 crore.
Manappuram Finance fell 4% during the session, contributing to sectoral weakness.
whatHappening: Indian benchmark indices NIFTY50 and SENSEX extended their rally for the third straight week.
PSU Banks emerged as the top sectoral gainers in the weekly market wrap.
Global tech sentiment was impacted by Nvidia's worst week following Jensen Huang's exit.
Domestic airfares rose 50% in 15 days, leading Delhi traders' body to seek Centre's intervention.
summary: In the last trading session, Indian benchmark indices closed lower with Sensex falling over 300 points due to inflation and crude oil pressures. Despite Friday's drop, both Sensex and Nifty extended gains for the third consecutive week, led by PSU banks. Stock-specific action saw Tata Motors report a Q2 net loss while Manappuram Finance slid 4%.
